newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriots protest at British base.
newsitem.headline: Cypriots protest at British base.

text.p: Scores of Greek Cypriots hurled stones and set fire to tyres outside a police station in a British military base on Sunday, demanding that a Greek teenager jailed for traffic offences be released, witnesses said.
The authorities of the British bases in Cyprus said that around 50 people, mainly youths, "engaged in mob activity" outside the police station in the south eastern Dhekelia base on Sunday afternoon.
Protestors were demanding the release of 17-year-old George Dimitri Kyriakos who is serving a three month sentence at a jail in Dhekelia, one of two British sovereign bases on the island.
"They gathered outside and threw stones, burnt tyres, set fire to trees next to the police station and generally engaged in mob activity," a bases spokesman told Reuters.
Earlier in the day, protesters had gathered outside the police station but many left after a personal appeal by Kyriakos's father Dimitri to disperse.
"I was reassured by the foreign minister the child would be released," he told reporters, adding the procedure would take two to three days.
The base authorities have said they are examining a plea for clemency from the family of the youth, who started serving his sentence on March 6.
Britain has retained two military bases in Cyprus since independence in 1960. A police force is empowered to prosecute any offender within bases territory.
Many Cypriots do not recognise the authority of the British bases in passing judgement on them.
Demonstrators hooked Greek and Cypriot flags on a blacked-out sign of the British crown opposite the police station.
"This isn't just for George. There are many others who get the same treatment," said local deputy Marios Matsakis, who took part in the demonstration.
"Courts of the bases are illegal and their (bases) police has no juristiction other than to safeguard military installations."
